_why: What a correct answer looks like, for THIS corpus. Deliberately not the catalog's `expect`: samples-catalog.json describes the TypeScript scenarios, and these ask different questions -- its 02 is system='Reply with only PONG' while this one asks for the capital of France, and its 10 is code execution while this one is a web search. Judging these cells against those patterns marks working cells as content mismatches, which is measured, not feared: it reported SOFT on 02, 03, 09 and 10 in a live sweep before this file existed.
_how: Keyed by the scenario id -- the filename up to the first underscore, so `29b` is its own entry. Values are regular expressions, applied case-insensitively. A scenario with NO entry is judged as before, on a non-empty answer alone: an absent expectation is honest about not knowing, where a guessed one would invent failures. Every pattern below is derived from the scenario's own prompt, its stub tool's return value, or the fixture file it reads.
_absent: 16, 17, 23, 26, 28 and 30 have no entry: every one of them currently stops at an unported name, so there is no observed answer to write a pattern from. Adding a guess would be inventing a criterion rather than recording one. 04b, 29b and 10b are entries in their own right because the runner keys on the full id.

_notes.15: Budgeted at 256 tokens rather than 32. Measured 2026-09-06 the model answered `The word spoken in the audio is` and stopped -- the budget ran out before the word, which reads as a failed transcription.
_notes.10b: Asks for a DOWNLOADABLE file, not just a saved one. A model told to `save them to fib.txt` writes it inside the sandbox and emits no artifact, so `result.files` is correctly 0 and the cell looks like the library dropped the files.
_notes.19: The catalog's own prompt (`If 2x=10 what is x?`), not the bat-and-ball problem this corpus used to ask. That is a cognitive trap, and a small model answers it inconsistently at any effort -- measured live 2026-09-06: the same model at effort=low returned 0.05, then 0.10, then 0.05. A cell that fails half the time on the model's mood cannot say whether reasoning reached the wire, which is what the scenario is for.
_notes.20: Requires a NON-ZERO cached token count: `cached:0` means the cache never took, which is the one thing this scenario exists to show. Measured 2026-09-03: anthropic 4411, openai 3840, xai 4160, openrouter 3840, google 0. Four of five non-zero is what says the plumbing works -- Gemini's implicit caching is best-effort and simply did not take on those two calls. Not a library defect.
_notes.25: Two answers, both correct: OpenAI realtime replies in TEXT and Gemini Live is audio-native -- it REFUSES a text-only session outright, so the scenario asks each for what it does and the audio side reports the byte count it received. Measured 2026-09-04: openai `Paris.`, google `audio:43202`.
_notes.31: Expect this one to be flaky, for the same reason as 27: the model decides whether to call the retrieval tool at all. The corpus itself is fine -- measured live 2026-09-06 over ten runs, `wait_indexed` reported ready with 1/1 indexed every time, and one run FOUND the document and then declined eight seconds later on the same corpus, which no indexing race explains. The document names an invented part (`Zorblatt regulator`) rather than a plausible one, because a model that might reasonably not know a real thing declines instead of searching: measured 2/5 with a generic name against 4/5 with the invented one.
_notes.27: Judged on citations rather than the version number, which changes with the world; grounding is what the scenario is about. Expect this one to be flaky: the model sometimes answers from its own knowledge without searching at all. Probed live 2026-09-03 -- one run parsed 0 citations with no annotations on the wire, the next parsed 1 with the url_citation present. The SDK reads them correctly; the model chooses whether to ground.
